sections.h2: Buying grain in a dip lifts contribution per kilolitre to Rs 14,178

chart.title: Integrated plant earns Rs 14,178 per kilolitre against Rs 7,722 for a pure plant
chart.sub: Contribution, Rs per kilolitre of ethanol, all-India prices, DDGS at Rs 13/kg.
chart.source: This blog's model; Agmarknet; BPCL e-tender 26985.

sections.means: Buying half the year's maize in a price dip and reselling the spare puts the integrated plant well ahead per kilolitre.
sections.todo: Stock up only when the price is at least 15% below its trailing 12-month mean and arrivals are surging.

sections.h2: The trading desk gains in a real dip and loses when buying at harvest prices

chart.title: Integrated plant gains Rs 45.6 crore a year in the glut and loses Rs 13.6 crore in 2024-25
chart.sub: Integrated minus pure plant EBITDA, Rs crore a year, at 70% allocation.

sections.means: The integrated plant gained Rs 45.6 crore a year in the 2025-26 glut but fell behind when it bought at harvest prices in 2024-25.
sections.todo: Buy ahead only in a real dip, and otherwise buy just the 30 to 45 days of maize the plant will use.

sections.h2: Owned silos cost Rs 728 to Rs 1,456 a quintal, so rented storage is the cheaper route

chart.title: Owning silos for two to four years costs Rs 728 to Rs 1,456 a quintal of maize used
chart.sub: Storage cost per quintal of maize used, 200 KLPD plant, all-India base case.

sections.means: Owned silos cost far more than a season of rented warehouse space, which the post prices at about Rs 10 a quintal a month.
sections.todo: Rent warehouse space for one season rather than building silos to hold grain for years.
